content:
If you've recently picked up a new Mac, like the just-released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you're probably also on the hunt for a new external display.

Below are my recommendations, spanning multiple product categories, price points, and more.

Best Mac external displays

Apple Studio Display

You simply can't talk about the best monitors on the market without mentioning Apple's Studio Display. While it carries a premium price tag, it features beautiful Apple design and comes with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View
  • True Tone: Automatically adjusts display color temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in several configurations at different price points, which I'll list below. If you're looking for an iMac-like experience, the Apple Studio Display is the obvious choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR launched earlier this year with several major advantages over the regular Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR, up to 2,000 nits peak HDR
  • Color support: Wide P3 and Adobe RGB color gamuts, 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz with Adaptive Sync
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, those advantages come at a price that's higher than the regular Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor is an appealing option for Mac users because it features a 4K OLED panel. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn has switched to this monitor and said it's been "a joy to pair with my Mac mini over the past few months."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2x USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

While it won't deliver the crisp 5K or 6K resolution of some models on the list, you'll enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks and superior color reproduction and contrast.

Where to buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K represents the evolution of LG's high-end ambitions in the display business. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels and a generous port selection. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • True Tone: None; auto-brightness support
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

Where to buy the LG UltraFine 6K

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin tried this monitor out in person and it immediately caught my eye. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K display delivers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) as the Studio Display in a similar 27-inch form factor, but at roughly half the price.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustments: Ambient light and backlight sensors auto-adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Watch Jeff's full review for all the details. If you're in the market for a 5K display for your Mac, the Asus ProArt is hard to beat.

Where to buy the Asus ProArt Display 5K:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you want something bigger and higher resolution, Asus has you covered there too. The new Asus ProArt Display 6K (PA32QCV) features a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly great value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connections, and headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

The ASUS ProArt 6K Display's biggest selling point might just be its pricing. It's significantly cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K displays on the market.

Where to buy the ASUS ProArt 6K display:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

The Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K is another appealing option to pair with your new Mac, also offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustments: Adaptive Picture auto-adjusts brightness based on ambient light
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Where to buy the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Monitor

This one might be my current favorite option. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes packed with a suite of Mac-friendly features, with the sharp 5K resolution being the standout.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: Typical and peak 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with customizable controls

Where to buy the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor:

Read our full review: BenQ 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 designer monitor is a true Apple Studio Display competitor

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor

If you want a 32-inch display to pair with your new Mac and your budget is under $1,000, this is one of the most compelling options. The biggest downside, though, is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. However, it offers a generous selection of ports, and the 32-inch panel comes in under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustments: No auto ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Where to buy the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor:

Read our full review: Are 32-inch 4K Mac monitors really not worth considering?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Monitor

If you want to go the ultrawide route for your Mac, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options out there. It delivers 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate across a 40-inch display, along with a generous port selection, a matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz with VRR support
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustments: Ambient light sensor auto-adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio out
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Where to buy the Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Monitor:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

A more affordable way to enter the ultrawide market is the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC, which is currently on sale at nearly half price. It doesn't come with all the bells and whistles of the other options, but you still get a 34-inch ultrawide curved display and a generous port selection, including a Thunderbolt 4 port with power delivery.

  • Display: 34-inch ultrawide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature, for an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits.
  • Webcam: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Where to buy the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC:

Wrap up

These are just some of the best options for pairing an external display with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, generous connectivity options, and unique sizes and form factors.

Did you recently pick up a new Mac? What display are you using to pair with it? Drop us a note in the comments.
